open_points.subject: record_change handling of an existing StoredValue
open_points.text: - record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs, a run's resumptions — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.
open_points.other_text: - record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.
open_points.question: Must every StoredValue listed by a change be written, or is an already-existing StoredValue explicitly exempt from the all-listed-records-must-be-written rule?
